requirements.text: Build Verisearch.slnx on .NET 10 with nullable analysis and warnings-as-errors enabled.
Preserve a sealed LedgerRow record, a nullable LedgerRow? Parse method, and a named Reconcile method so parsing and accumulation remain separate.

The evaluator supplies at most 10,000 LF-delimited segments that are nonempty before CR handling; larger inputs are outside this contract. LF is the only delimiter and a final unterminated segment is processed. Discard only segments whose length is already zero, then remove one trailing CR from each retained segment; therefore a segment containing only CR becomes an empty malformed record and counts toward the bound, while any other CR is data. A valid record is exactly <identifier><separator><amount>, with no quoting, escaping, or surrounding whitespace. An identifier is 1-16 ASCII characters: an uppercase A-Z first, then only uppercase A-Z, digits, or underscore. Amount is one or more ASCII digits, leading zeroes are allowed, signs, whitespace, non-ASCII digits, and values above Int32.MaxValue are rejected. Add duplicate-key amounts in a Dictionary<string,long>; a malformed record never erases valid state.

The supplied constants are this candidate's fixed compile-time assignment; no runtime mode switch is required. Write exactly six lines: domain={{domain}}; policy={{failure-mode}}; order={{output-order}}; entries=every accepted key and its accumulated amount as comma-separated KEY:TOTAL pairs in ordinal {{output-order}} key order (or exactly entries= when none are accepted); total=the checked Int64 sum of all per-key totals; invalid={{failure-mode}} when at least one record is malformed, otherwise invalid=none. The 10,000-line bound makes each per-key total and the grand total non-overflowing.

rubric.criterion: The assigned behavioral contract is satisfied by a clean build and varied runs.

brief: Build a self-contained {{domain}} keyed quantity ledger, unrelated to source verification. The executable reads records only from standard input. Its literal separator is '{{input-shape}}', malformed-record status word is {{failure-mode}}, and per-key output order is ordinal {{output-order}}. These are fixed candidate constants rather than runtime choices. The public requirements fully define identifier and numeric syntax, bounds, newline rules, duplicate handling, malformed input, and the six-line output; no arguments or external files are used.
publicExamples: For separator '|', BAY_2|0005 is lexically valid; bay|5, BAY|+5, and BAY| 5 are malformed.
Every distinct accepted identifier must appear with its own accumulated total, so a scalar grand-total-only implementation is insufficient.
The rationale is part of the submission, but the public prompt intentionally does not supply its trace or mutation evidence.
title: {{domain}} keyed ledger
